host.name: zbook
host.gpu: AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 40 CU, unified LPDDR5X)
host.note: Every figure is gfx1151. No gfx1100 hardware was available.

change: The softmax weights were stored row-major -- [row][key] with the row stride taken from the runtime block size -- so one key's weights for eight rows cost eight index computations (r * blockDim.x against a runtime blockDim.x) and eight shared-memory requests, and every lane paid that per key. They are now stored key-major ([key][row], eight consecutive floats per key), so the row index is a compile-time offset inside an unrolled loop, one base address serves the whole row block, and the block arrives in two 16-byte requests.
why: The kernel's address arithmetic had grown as large as its math: rocprofv3 --pmc on the previous kernel counts 3829 scalar-ALU instructions per lane-tile against 9060 vector-ALU, so a runtime-strided index into shared memory was costing as much as the arithmetic it fed.

instruction_counts_per_lane_tile.command: rocprofv3 --pmc SQ_INSTS_VALU SQ_INSTS_SALU SQ_INSTS_LDS SQ_INSTS_FLAT (dispatch 1, 228624 lane-tiles per call)
instruction_counts_per_lane_tile.note: Counters are deterministic and unaffected by the host's clock drift, so this is the primary evidence for the change; the wall-clock pair below is the secondary check.

paired_kernel_ab.command: python3 scripts/yue2_attention_bench.py --repeat 40, alternating the two sources in one session
paired_kernel_ab.note: Seventeen percent fewer instructions buys 3.9% of wall clock, which is what a kernel at ~75% of its issue limit with the rest in stalls can show. Absolute times drift up to 15% between batches on this host, so only the paired ratio is claimed.

paired_replay_ab.command: python3 scripts/yue2_e2e_gate.py --only mandarin-off-s1234 --steps 2 --skip-live, alternating the two sources

rows_per_block_recheck.conclusion: Eight rows stays the optimum. The cheaper per-row shared-memory traffic does not make sixteen rows viable, because the register and shared-memory footprint of the accumulators is what fails at that width.

bit_parity.result: bit-identical to the parent kernel (max abs diff 0.0)

next_candidates: Scalar-ALU is still 3091 per lane-tile against 8066 vector-ALU. The accumulation loop now spends one base address per key, so the remaining bulk is the two key walks' pointer stepping and the tile-loop bookkeeping; that is a smaller prize than this change was.

Closing the rest of the gap to the reference needs the register-blocked layout, where a lane holds several keys' dot products and the softmax reductions move to shuffles. That changes arithmetic and therefore needs the profile gates rather than bit parity.
